name: Spermidine

lead: Spermidine is a naturally occurring polyamine present in all cells and in foods such as wheat germ, soybeans, mushrooms and aged cheese. It is sold as a supplement, often as wheat germ extract.

It is promoted as an autophagy-inducing longevity compound. Observational data link higher dietary intake to lower mortality, but randomized human evidence is preliminary and no cosmetic benefit has been established.

paras: Spermidine induces autophagy in model organisms, partly through inhibition of the acetyltransferase EP300, and is required for hypusination of eIF5A, which supports mitochondrial function and immune cell activity.

Generally well tolerated at studied intakes; mild gastrointestinal effects are possible. Polyamines are also needed by rapidly growing cells, so theoretical concerns exist in cancer settings. Legal as a supplement or novel food in many regions.
